methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops targeting community access in Hampton Roads represent grassroots capacity-building that could distribute deep capability through peer networks, directly countering platform-dependent shallow adoption.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's partnership with AI Ready RVA creates institutional infrastructure for distributed AI education beyond NoVA's corporate ecosystem, potentially seeding deep capability in Virginia's second-tier metro hub through community-oriented training.

signals.title: TAYLOR: AI data centers increase Virginia’s urban-rural divide - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: Data center concentration in NoVA creates economic and infrastructural asymmetry that entrenches urban-rural divide, with AI's physical infrastructure deepening geographic inequality rather than distributing capability.

signals.title: New artificial intelligence minor launches this fall - Virginia Tech News
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech's new AI minor concentrates deep technical capability in an established academic hub, but statewide reach depends on whether graduates disperse regionally or migrate to NoVA/Richmond metro corridors.

signals.title: Tony Stark’s J.A.R.V.I.S., meet Amelia, Norfolk Naval Shipyard’s IT AI help assistant - MilitaryNews.com
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk Naval Shipyard's deployment of Amelia, an AI IT assistant, represents platform-delivered shallow adoption where users consume AI tools without building underlying capability, typical of military-bureaucratic technology implementation.
